prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the receding asphalt road plane (brightest at 1–3 m at the bottom edge), the raised sidewalk, wall, and overhead streetlamps along the right edge (3–12 m away in frames 1–4), and the grassy median with utility boxes, shrubs, and background houses (dark grey to black at >25 m) on the left. As the camera wearer moves forward and turns left across frames 1 to 5, two pedestrians walking side-by-side (0.5–1 m apart, with a man on the left and a woman on the right) and a brown dog 1–1.5 m in front-left of them on the left curb approach from roughly 25–30 m away in frame 1 to 12–15 m in frame 3 and 6–8 m ahead-left in frame 5. From the RGB context, both walkers and the dog face and move toward the left side of the scene (away from the intersection and not looking toward the camera wearer), with the woman partially occluding the man's right side in earlier frames and holding a leash within her arm's reach while nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer (whose body is out of view below the frame). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes of the two walkers, the dog, and the right-side lamp posts from the sunlit background houses in frames 3–5 and shows the continuous ground-plane distance gradient during the left turn. However, the map is unreliable at long range in frames 1–2 where the pedestrians and dog blend into background depth, omits thin structures like the leashes, and flattens each person into a uniform-depth silhouette that hides facing direction and limb positions.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few discrete foreground and mid-ground objects on a black background as the camera wearer advances along the road and turns left across the 5 frames: the two pedestrians on the left sidewalk (approaching from ~25–30 m in frame 1 to ~6–8 m in frame 5, spaced 0.5–1 m apart) and a white SUV ('car') parked in a driveway to their right (~35–40 m away in frame 1, closing to ~20–25 m and shifting to the right side of the frame by frame 5 as the camera turns left). In the RGB context, the man walks slightly ahead-left of the woman and a brown dog walks 1–1.5 m ahead-left of them on a leash within the walkers' arm's reach, with all three facing toward the left edge of the frame away from the camera wearer while nothing is within the camera wearer's reach. The segmentation map makes it easy to track the lateral displacement between the pedestrians on the left and the parked car shifting right across frames 2–5 without background clutter, and shows the overlapping boundary where the woman on the right partially occludes the man beside her in frames 4–5. However, it is highly unreliable for full spatial understanding: it completely misses the road, curbs, walls, lamp posts, houses, and the dog (while falsely splitting/duplicating a third 'person' mask onto the man's outstretched arm and dog region in frame 5), and fails to detect the pedestrians in frame 2 or the man in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (all black) across all 5 frames, detecting no body joints or hand keypoints anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, two pedestrians walk side-by-side (0.5–1 m apart) with a dog 1–1.5 m ahead-left of them along the left curb—closing from roughly 25–30 m in frame 1 to 6–8 m in frame 5 as the camera wearer approaches and turns left—while facing toward the left away from the camera wearer with their hands holding leashes within arm's reach. Meanwhile, the camera wearer's own body and hands remain entirely out of view below the bottom edge of the wide-angle frame, with no objects within arm's reach. Because the pose estimator fails completely on the small, distant pedestrian figures and the unviewed ego-body, this map provides no spatial information beyond what is in the RGB image and is entirely unreliable for determining positions, facing directions, gaze, occlusions, or reachability in this sequence.
